scenarios.name: Successful topic search
scenarios.expected: Returns a non-empty list; each result includes document_id, title, and source_url

scenarios.name: Search with agency filter
scenarios.expected: Returns results scoped to the specified agency, each with source_url

scenarios.name: Search yields no results
scenarios.expected: Returns an empty list with a clear 'no matches found' message; no error thrown

scenarios.name: Empty search term rejected
scenarios.expected: Validation error returned before any API call; clear message

scenarios.name: Retrieve valid document
scenarios.expected: Returns full metadata: title, document_type, agency_id, docket_id, source_url

scenarios.name: Retrieve nonexistent document
scenarios.expected: Clear 'document not found' message; no crash; graceful 404 handling

scenarios.name: Invalid document ID format rejected
scenarios.expected: Validation error before API call; clear message

scenarios.name: Retrieve valid docket
scenarios.expected: Returns docket title, agency_id, docket_type, source_url

scenarios.name: Retrieve nonexistent docket
scenarios.expected: Clear 'docket not found' message; graceful 404 handling

scenarios.name: Comment requirements — open period
scenarios.expected: Returns status='open', accepting_comments=true, a days_remaining count, and a populated comment_url
scenarios.note: Comment window closes 2026-09-09. Use FAA-2026-9967-0001 (closes 2026-10-17) if this scenario is re-run after that date.

scenarios.name: Comment requirements — closed with late comments accepted
scenarios.expected: Returns status='closed_late_comments_accepted' with days_since_closed; correctly overrides the contradictory openForComment=true flag

scenarios.name: Comment requirements — not applicable
scenarios.expected: Returns status='not_applicable' with comment_url suppressed to null

scenarios.name: Rate limit handling
scenarios.expected: All client functions raise RegulationsClientError with retry guidance; the error message does not echo the upstream response body
scenarios.note: Verified by mocking the HTTP layer rather than exhausting the live 1000-per-hour quota. See tests/test_rate_limit.py.

scenarios.name: Upstream 404 distinguished from general error
scenarios.expected: Raises DocumentNotFoundError, a subclass of RegulationsClientError, so a missing record can be handled specifically or generally

scenarios.name: Server error body truncated
scenarios.expected: Error message includes the status code but truncates the response body to 200 characters

scenarios.name: Request timeout configured
scenarios.expected: Every outbound request sets timeout=10

scenarios.name: Unauthorized raises client error
scenarios.expected: Raises RegulationsClientError rather than returning an empty result set

scenarios.name: End-to-end analyst workflow
scenarios.expected: Agent chains tools correctly, produces a cited summary with source URLs at each step

scenarios.name: Adversarial ID input rejected

input._payloads: path traversal, SQL syntax, script tags, parameter injection, null byte, header injection, JNDI lookup, oversized string

scenarios.expected: All 13 payloads rejected by the Pydantic ID pattern before any network call, for all three ID-taking tools
scenarios.note: Tool inputs originate from an LLM agent that may be acting on untrusted user text. See tests/test_adversarial_input.py.

scenarios.name: Bounded parameters cannot be driven out of range
scenarios.expected: All rejected by Pydantic bounds before any network call

scenarios.name: Search term accepts free text without pattern restriction
scenarios.expected: Accepted and treated as a parameter value, not an instruction; cannot alter request structure because base URL and parameter names are fixed in the client
scenarios.note: Deliberate design decision. Restricting search_term would break legitimate searches containing punctuation, and it is never used as a URL path segment.

scenarios.name: Latency consistency across repeated trials
scenarios.expected: Mean latency within the 5-second threshold; outcome identical across trials
scenarios.note: Single-run latency does not demonstrate stability. See measure_latency.py.
